summary: Tenant handshake throttle causing midday attach drought and degraded P99 throughput
description:
Issue summary: Customer QueryFlow reports sustained p99 latency regressions and sharp throughput drops for their dedicated pool during the 11:30-13:30 PST window. Symptoms look like a midday 'attach drought' where new allocation attempts fail or queue for long periods, causing request queuing and increased tail latency. Impact: Customer-facing endpoints see ~3-5x p99 increase and a 30-60% throughput reduction for routed model redwood/opt-1.3b. This is affecting production traffic and violating their internal SLOs.

Environment: Dedicated capacity (reserved cluster) in us-west-2. Autoscaling enabled with predictive warmup. No recent customer-side config changes reported.

Observed behavior: - New request attach attempts time out or backoff repeatedly for a sustained period. - Autoscaler does not return capacity quickly enough; cluster show high attach-retry counts. - Background prefetch/pin tasks spike CPU and NVMe I/O on a subset of hosts. - A small cohort of tenants exhibit long-lived handshake latency that holds allocator slots open.

Expected behavior: - Attach attempts should find free slots or trigger predictive spin-up within configured cooldown window. - Autoscaler should replenish capacity to keep p99 within targets.

Initial logs/metrics attached (snippets): - allocator.attach_retries: 842 spikes between 11:32-12:10 - prefetch_io_ops/s: host-rt-07: 12k -> baseline 900 - nvme_io_wait_ms: host-rt-07: p95 450ms - kernel_queue_depth: host-rt-07 elevated - per-tenant-conn-latency: tenant-queryflow-03: p99 1.2s (baseline 120ms)

Timeline: 2026-03-10 11:28: QueryFlow reports slowdown. 11:35: Support triage. 11:50: SRE review of allocator and autoscaler dashboards. 12:05: Temporary mitigation applied (soft cap on prefetch threads for the noisy tenant).

Notes: This looks different from classic noisy-GPU compute saturation: the hosts implicated show moderate GPU utilization but heavy NVMe IO and long attach handshakes. Hypothesis is that handshake resource contention (prefetch + metadata writes) is preventing slot recycling and causing allocator starvation across the pool.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Route synthetic steady-load traffic for redwood/opt-1.3b through a dedicated pool with autoscale enabled.
2) Simulate a tenant that opens many long-lived connections with prefix caching enabled and forces aggressive prefetch operations (high kv-cache churn).
3) Observe allocator.attach_retries and host nvme_io_wait metrics during the ramp to midday traffic levels.
4) Correlate p99 latency and attach queue lengths with host-side prefetch_io_ops spikes.
comments: 2026-03-10 11:36 - Maya Chen (Support): Thanks for the report. We've escalated to SRE and will validate allocator metrics. Can you confirm whether you've recently enabled any prefetch/keepalive changes?

2026-03-10 11:48 - Customer (QueryFlow - Alyssa Rivera): No config changes on our side. We did start a long-running batch that keeps many model contexts warm starting 11:00 PST but that's expected traffic.

2026-03-10 11:52 - Devon Patel (SRE): Looking at metrics now. Host host-rt-07 shows nvme stall and prefetch saturation. GPUs are not saturated; attach path is stalling on IO. Opening investigation notes.

2026-03-10 12:03 - Devon Patel (SRE): Applied temporary mitigation: reduced prefetch concurrency for tenant-queryflow-03 via policy override. Attach retries dropped by ~40% in first 5 mins. Continuing to monitor.
2026-03-11 09:22 - Maya Chen (Support): Customer reports recurrence yesterday during same window albeit milder. Raising to engineering for durable mitigation and scheduler-level throttles.

2026-03-12 08:15 - Engineering (Priya Rao): Reproduced locally with synthetic prefetch client. Found allocator backpressure code path that holds slot while metadata write completes. PR suggested to fast-fail long metadata writes and let autoscaler supply warm slots earlier.
investigation_notes: - Correlation found between per-host nvme_io_wait and global attach_retries count; host-rt-07, host-rt-09 most affected.
- No driver-level GPU errors observed; GPU SM/util consistent with moderate inference load (45-65%).
- Prefetch subsystem triggered high small-file NVMe writes (checkpoint-like behavior) from a single tenant's long-lived warmers.
- Allocator code holds a slot until metadata commit completes; when metadata IO is delayed, slot remains unusable and autoscaler sees high allocation pressure.
- Autoscaler telemetry shows spin-up latency within expected band, but attach handshakes still queue because existing slots are logically blocked.
- Reproduced with a synthetic client that issues aggressive KV-cache refreshes: identical attach drought observed in a scaled test cluster.
resolution_notes: Mitigation applied (2026-03-10 12:03): Reduced prefetch concurrency for the noisy tenant which reduced nvme_io_wait and lowered attach retries by ~40%.

Short-term fix (2026-03-12): Rolled out autoscaler config change to add an allocator backoff fast-path: long metadata writes will fast-fail with retry backoff instead of holding slots indefinitely. Deployed to prod-us-west canary (20% of pool) during low-risk window.

Long-term remediation: Engineering to land PR to change allocator slot lifecycle so metadata commits are performed asynchronously and slot handoff occurs on logical commit acceptance. Also evaluating per-tenant prefetch rate-limiting at the scheduler layer and improving telemetry alerting on nvme_io_wait spikes.

Customer communication: Informed QueryFlow of temporary mitigation and that a short-term autoscaler change is rolling out to canary. Recommended customer to throttle internal warmers if feasible as a stop-gap.
Follow-ups: - Post-deploy verification window 2026-03-13 11:00-14:00 PST. - Create INT ticket to track allocator refactor (INT-90045). - Add NVMe IO wait alert to runbook.
